questions.stem: A technician needs to check for bad sectors on a hard drive and recover any readable data from them. Which command should they run?
questions.explanation: chkdsk /r locates bad sectors and recovers readable data, and implies /f.
questions.trap: chkdsk /f only fixes file system errors; it does not scan sectors.

questions.stem: A user reports a corporate web app times out intermittently. Other internal sites work fine. Which command BEST identifies where in the network path the slowdown happens?
questions.explanation: pathping maps the path AND runs per-hop statistics, so you can see which hop is dropping packets or adding latency.
questions.trap: ping confirms reachability but does not tell you WHERE the problem is on the path.

questions.stem: Suspecting malware, a tech wants to see which Windows executables are responsible for each open network connection. Which command?
questions.explanation: netstat -b shows the executable that owns each connection. Requires elevation.
questions.trap: netstat -a shows all connections including listening, but does not map them to executables.

questions.stem: After a tech edits a Group Policy at the domain controller, the change is not visible on a workstation. The user is logged in. What is the fastest way to apply the new policy without forcing a logout?
questions.explanation: gpupdate /force reapplies all group policies immediately. gpresult /r only reports what is currently applied; it doesn't refresh anything.
questions.trap: gpresult shows applied policies; it does NOT refresh them.

questions.stem: Critical Windows OS files appear to have been replaced by an installer. Which command can verify and repair the OS files?
questions.explanation: sfc /scannow (System File Checker) verifies and replaces corrupted or modified protected Windows files. Log written to cbs.log.
questions.trap: chkdsk /r examines the disk for bad sectors; it does not verify OS file integrity.

questions.stem: A scheduled overnight script must copy a 50 GB archive to a remote site over an unreliable link. Which utility is the BEST choice?
questions.explanation: robocopy ('robust copy') automatically retries failed segments and supports bandwidth throttling - exactly what an unreliable WAN link needs.
questions.trap: copy /v verifies, but a single dropped packet still fails the transfer with no retry.

questions.stem: Before issuing a remote shutdown command, a technician wants to make absolutely sure they are connected to the correct machine. Which command confirms the machine identity?
questions.explanation: hostname prints the local computer name. The classic sanity check before destructive commands on a remote session.
questions.trap: whoami prints the user, not the machine. winver shows the OS version.

questions.stem: Match each Windows network command to its primary purpose.

pairs.rightText: Show IP / subnet / gateway / DNS for each adapter
Map the routers between you and a destination
Query DNS for a name or address
Map a network share to a drive letter

questions.explanation: These five are the Windows networking CLI staples. Memorize what symptom each one diagnoses.

questions.stem: A user on a workstation reports they cannot reach an internal web app. Order these troubleshooting commands in the sequence that builds from local config out to the path.

items.text: tracert or pathping to the app to see where the path breaks

questions.explanation: Start local (own config), then prove the gateway works, then prove DNS works, then prove the destination is reachable, then map the path.
questions.trap: Jumping straight to tracert. If DNS is broken, tracert by name will fail in a misleading way.

questions.stem: Which of the following commands REQUIRE administrator privileges? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: chkdsk /f, format, and netstat -b all need elevation. ipconfig (read-only) does not.
questions.trap: ipconfig alone is read-only and works as a standard user. Anything that modifies state or reads protected info typically needs admin.
